steps.title: Read the page
steps.body: Analytics, session recordings, support tickets, and whatever sales gets asked twice a week. Most of what you need is usually already inside the company before anyone runs anything.

steps.title: Write it down before running it
steps.body: Hypothesis, metric, sample size, duration, stopping rule. All of it agreed before the variant gets built, so that when the result comes in there is nothing left to argue about except what to do next.

steps.title: Turn the result into a brief
steps.body: Most tests lose. Kohavi's published base rate is roughly one in three ideas improving its target metric. So the write-up matters more than the result: a loss you can explain still changes what gets built next, and plenty of wins can't be explained at all.

faq.question: Have you done this for a real client?
faq.answer: No. Everything on this page is self-initiated and labelled that way on every case. What I'd point you at instead is the reasoning: each project shows the territories I rejected and why, what the research came back with, and where a hypothesis broke. You can tell more about someone's judgement from the work they threw out than from the work that survived, and that is usually the part a spec portfolio leaves out.

faq.question: You're applying for two different jobs.
faq.answer: At a company with no dedicated experimentation owner, which by Speero's benchmark is roughly 40% of brands, these are one job: somebody still has to decide what to test and what the result means for the creative. At a large agency with a planning department and a separate CRO function they're two jobs, and I'd apply for one of them. If you're the second kind of employer, the link you were sent only shows the relevant role.

faq.question: How many tests have you actually run?
faq.answer: Not many. I'd be suspicious of a junior who said otherwise, and so should you be. Published base rates put experiment success at around one in three, dropping to 10% to 20% in domains that have already been optimised hard, so a junior showing five wins and no losses is either working from a very small sample or has picked what to show you. There's an access problem underneath that as well: Google sunset Optimize in September 2023, and with it went the free way of accumulating real tests without already having the job that hands you the traffic. What does transfer is how I prioritise, how I decide a test is finished, what I do with a site that will never reach significance, and one test I got wrong. All of that is on this page.

faq.question: What's your stopping rule?
faq.answer: Sample size and duration are set before the variant is built, worked out from the baseline conversion rate and the smallest effect that would be worth acting on. Minimum one full business cycle, usually two weeks, so weekday and weekend traffic are both represented. No peeking at partial results to decide whether to keep going. And if the test reaches its duration without reaching the planned sample, it gets recorded as inconclusive and stays that way, instead of running on until the numbers happen to look like something.

faq.question: How do you prioritise?
faq.answer: [FILL: your actual framework in three sentences. Name it, say what you score on, and say what you do when a stakeholder wants a test that scores badly. The last part is the one you'll be asked about.]

faq.question: What if the site doesn't have enough traffic to test?
faq.answer: Most don't. Running a smaller version of the same test doesn't fix that, so the method has to change: session replay, support-ticket themes, five user interviews, sitting in on sales calls, a painted-door test on one element. What that gives you is direction, which is a weaker claim than significance, and the job is then to say which of the two you're holding. Reporting a 15% lift off 40 conversions is how people get caught.

faq.question: What does the 30-day guarantee mean?
faq.answer: A prioritised test roadmap in week one, with the ranking method written down so you can argue with it. A stopping rule applied to whatever is already running, including a call on anything that should be stopped now. A research pass that doesn't depend on having traffic. One experiment designed, built, shipped and analysed end to end. And one written brief saying what the result means for what gets made next.
